cross_references.relationship: tolling exceptions — §583.340 defines the only circumstances that toll the five-year clock: impossibility, impracticability, or futility of bringing the action to trial; stays; court-ordered suspensions. Without §583.340, the five-year rule would be absolutely inflexible.

cross_references.relationship: computation and dismissal — §583.360 governs how the five years is calculated (from filing, not service) and mandates dismissal on motion or the court's own motion when the period expires.
cross_references.build_status: NOT BUILT AS STANDALONE STANDARD — computation and dismissal procedures documented within ccp_583_310 reasoning layer.

cross_references.relationship: policy tension — §583.130 declares California's preference for trial on the merits. The five-year rule (§583.310) is the mandatory exception: when the two policies conflict, the five-year dismissal controls. The Legislature values finality over merits resolution after five years.

cross_references.relationship: procedural deadline sibling — §340.5 determines when a medical malpractice case must be FILED. §583.310 determines when it must be TRIED. Together they define the outer boundary of a medical malpractice case's lifespan.
